newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour plans group to prepare for EU presidency.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour plans group to prepare for EU presidency.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party said on Sunday it would, if elected, set up a working group of government ministers and business representatives to prepare for the UK's six-month presidency of the European Union in 1998.

Labour's finance spokesman Gordon Brown said the plans would be included in the party's newly released election manifesto to business leaders. He said UK employers group, the Confederation of British Industry, has already agreed to be involved.
"This shows both business and government can work together both in Britain and Europe to achieve common aims," Brown told the BBC in an interview on Sunday.

Brown said the working group would look at a number of areas, including energy, telecommunications and financial services, where Europe needs to open markets further to enhance the single market. It would also look at ways of increasing flexibility, productivity and employment across Europe, he said.
"We're getting away from the old idea that public (sector) has got to say one thing and private has to say another and there's never any proper relationship between them."
The Labour Party is currently more than 25 percentage points ahead of the ruling Conservatives in opinion polls, with just over a month to the May 1 election.

In the same interview, Brown declined to name the specific utility companies which would be liable to pay Labour's planned windfall tax -- a one-off tax on privatised utilities aimed at raising at least three billion pounds for job-creation schemes.
"The companies that are affected and will be considered for this tax are those companies which have been privatised and are licensed and regulated by statute," Brown told the BBC.

The Independent on Sunday said U.S. corporations which own stakes in UK regional electricity companies are lobbying U.S. politicians to retaliate against any move by a UK Labour government to impose such a windfall tax.
